context: The data is this plugin's own bundled mock: the sources, records and keys are fixed in the plugin package (fixtures/sources.json and fixtures/credentials.json), every run is identical, and no network or environment variables change anything. The fixture holds three sources: `acme-readings` (hourly weather readings), `acme-stations` (station registry) and `globex-claims` (open claims). Your input names two of them; exactly one can be reached with a credential ref, the other is blocked because the ref it accepts is not set. A source may list more than one ref in `list_credential_refs` output: one may be set but revoked (`connect` rejects it and says so), and a revoked ref never unblocks a source. Connect to each source with the refs listed for it, in the order listed, until one opens or none is left. `fetch_records` pages through the connected source: first call with cursor null, then with each `next_cursor` until it is null; a page may first fail with 'temporarily unavailable (HTTP 503)' and then serve on a retry with the same cursor, so never skip a page. A record may appear again on a later page (same id); count each distinct id once. A record lacks a required field when the field is absent from its `fields`, or is null, or is `""`. `missing_fields` must list each required field some distinct record lacks, with how many distinct records lack it; records are counted once per field; order does not matter; it is empty when nothing is lacking. Report the two source ids with the reachable one as `reachable_source`, count all distinct records, list the missing fields, name as `unblock_credential` the exact credential-ref NAME (as `list_credential_refs` lists it) the blocked source accepts but that is not set, and write a one-or-two-sentence summary. Only credential ref names are ever handled: never write, guess, or ask for a key value, and never put one in the report.
